trigger: a later edit adds `#else` after the guard at depth 1, or a `// ... /*` comment later closed by `*/` after the final `#endif`
classification_rationale: absence of hardening in a self-declared best-effort tripwire; not a contradiction
summary: check_text() does not reject `#else`/`#elif` at depth 1 of the guard (the `#else` branch compiles under TSan) and strip_comments() strips block comments before line comments so code between `// ...` `/*` and a later `*/` is swallowed. Both reproduced by security-guardian on crafted scratch inputs; quality-engineer reproduced the `#else` mutant (exit 0). Realistic-ness: contrived. Consequence of a miss is a LOUD nightly TSan compile break (the pre-fix state), never silent. Docstring already declares BEST-EFFORT TRIPWIRE, so not false assurance. Recommended disposition: optional fold (reject `#else`/`#elif` at depth 1; single-pass comment tokenizer) or file with sec-2/UP-2/con-1 as one hardening follow-up. Not blocking.

trigger: the marker comment is reflowed/re-wrapped (or deleted) in exactly ONE of the two marker files, optionally with code later appended after its closing #endif
classification_rationale: absence of hardening; the gate's own docstring discloses best-effort
summary: The marker is matched as one literal string and nothing pins the expected file set, so a re-wrapped marker silently un-checks a file; `checked==0` only fires when ALL files lose it. Reproduced three times: security-guardian crafted file (exit 0), quality-engineer mutant 'marker removed from one real file' (exit 0, 'checked 1'), chaos-injector CH-2a (marker re-wrapped in gate.cpp + code after #endif -> exit 0 'checked 1' = confirmed silent false green; both re-wrapped -> loud). Consequence: delayed LOUD nightly TSan compile failure, i.e. the pre-#6419 status quo; not silent in production, no product control involved. Recommended disposition: fold (whitespace/comment-star tolerant marker regex `Whole(?:\s|\*|/)+file...`, cheaper than count pinning which adds churn) or include in the PR-time -fsyntax-only follow-up. Not blocking.

trigger: someone appends a TEST_CASE after the guard's closing #endif
summary: The failure message names file, line, cause and first offending line but not the remedy. Proposed: append '; move it above that #endif, or drop the "Whole file compiled out under TSan" marker if the file is meant to be partly guarded'. happy-path verified the message is otherwise actionable. Recommended: fold (one-line string edit in a file already touched).

trigger: a reader sees 'no top-level `#ifndef YUZU_TSAN_BUILD` guard' for a file whose guard is nested/non-first
summary: Message says 'top-level' but the code accepts the first `#ifndef YUZU_TSAN_BUILD` at any nesting. Proposed: drop 'top-level'. Recommended: fold.

trigger: a reader maintaining the file tail
summary: The pre-existing `#endif` closing `#ifndef _WIN32` is unlabelled and now sits two lines above the new `#endif // YUZU_TSAN_BUILD`; the pair is easy to misread. Proposed: label the earlier one `#endif // _WIN32`. Optional fold.

trigger: a regression is introduced while the Big Tam pool is unhealthy (ci.yml linux job skipped as satisfied) or via a docs-only PR path
classification_rationale: a CI mirror step is absent; no required-doc item applies, hence not I7
summary: The new gate runs on PRs only via the ci.yml `linux` job `--suite docs` (ci.yml:1267; gated on bigtam_pool_healthy && code_changed; no path filter). Sibling docs-suite gates are mirrored in docs-lint.yml on a GitHub-hosted runner; this one is not. Windows/macOS legs exclude the docs suite (moot: source-text, OS-independent). SRE restated and accepted at LOW: recurrence is self-announcing (nightly TSan compile fails, nightly-broken opens). Optional follow-up: mirror in docs-lint.yml. Not blocking.

trigger: a maintainer reads tests/meson.build comment to learn which legs build with TSan
classification_rationale: imprecise enumeration in an otherwise true comment; wording-owned by docs-writer
summary: Comment says a case 'compiles everywhere except the nightly's TSan leg'. build-ci verified 'no PR job builds with TSan' is TRUE, but sanitizer-tests.yml's tsan job (workflow_dispatch) is a second TSan leg that also compiles the tests. Suggested wording: 'except the TSan legs (nightly.yml, sanitizer-tests.yml)'. Optional fold.

trigger: a future edit adds an early partial `#ifndef YUZU_TSAN_BUILD` above the real whole-file guard in a marker file
summary: Script checks the FIRST `#ifndef YUZU_TSAN_BUILD`. No such shape exists today (lines 52-59 are `#if defined`/`#define`).

trigger: early partial guard before the real guard (CH-1 variants 1a-1d)
summary: Gate 5 chaos-injector executed the mutants on scratch copies: only a FALSE RED (exit 1, fails closed; message in 1b points at the partial guard and masks the real defect). A false green is structurally impossible (an earlier guard with empty tail leaves no later guard; a later nested guard is truly excluded). Speculative claim resolved to verified: band stays LOW. Park/file with the hardening follow-up; optional message tweak.

trigger: a case is added INSIDE the guard that depends on a fixture/helper defined OUTSIDE the guard
classification_rationale: a PR-time TSan syntax check is absent; nightly still catches it loudly
summary: The gate defends only 'code after the closing #endif'. A case inside the guard using something defined outside it still breaks the TSan compile with no PR-time signal. chaos-injector CH-3 showed a bare UP-2 needs a second guard (which trips CH-1) so it reaches a silent green only combined with a lost marker (sec-2). Real fix = PR-time `g++ -fsyntax-only -D__SANITIZE_THREAD__` of marker files; out of scope for #6419. Recommended: file as ONE follow-up together with sec-1/sec-2/con-1/bci-1. Not blocking (loud nightly failure).

trigger: a case is added after the closing #endif of an unmarked structurally-whole-file-guarded file
classification_rationale: scope limit of an opt-in tripwire
summary: Gate is opt-in by prose marker. test_mcp_body_cap.cpp (72..304=EOF), test_security_headers.cpp (387..492=EOF), test_body_cap_policy.cpp (485..1137=EOF) are whole-tail-guarded but unmarked, so unchecked (all clean today, per unhappy-path tail reads). Same family as sec-2. Optional: note scope in the docstring, or cover via the PR-time syntax-check follow-up.

trigger: an author of a partly-guarded test file copies the marker phrasing
classification_rationale: in-code contract pointer absent; in-code prose never qualifies as a required doc (absence is of a pointer, not one of the six required docs), hence not I7
summary: 'A file that is only partly guarded on purpose must not carry the marker' is stated only in the python docstring; the two marker headers (gate.cpp:27, _pg.cpp:21) do not say the marker opts the file into the gate. Proposed: append '(checked by tests/test_tsan_whole_file_guard.py)' to both marker lines. Consequence of a miss is a loud, self-explaining gate failure. Optional fold.

trigger: the commit is pushed with its current trailer
classification_rationale: commit metadata wording; no product or audit effect
summary: Commit trailer reads `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`; the session attribution instruction names `Claude Sonnet 5.5` and a Claude-Session trailer. Raised independently by docs-writer (Gate 2) and consistency-auditor (con-2); compliance-officer (shown it) rates INFO, no repo rule pins a model, model identity of the producing session unverifiable here. Commit is unpushed, so the caller can amend before pushing. NOTE: the user's memory rule says no session link on PRs/issues/reviews. Caller decides.

trigger: the preprocessor-only change somehow alters non-TSan behaviour
summary: Producer did not do a non-TSan compile/run. Gate 2 proved byte-identical non-TSan token streams (45 TEST_CASEs both sides); quality-engineer ran a non-TSan -fsyntax-only (exit 0) and cpp-expert g++ -fsyntax-only with/without -fsanitize=thread (rc 0). Residual: full non-TSan link and run of the 45 cases not executed. Cannot occur since non-TSan preprocessing is identical. Optional: run `meson test --suite server` filtered to [csrf][same_site][pipeline] before push.
